claims.text: Replacing the EAM reference with an MTP and TI with FEP will reduce the computational cost of TaVCrW melting calculations by more than 80%.
The MTP+FEP method will maintain a free-energy accuracy of a few meV/atom relative to TOR-TILD for TaVCrW.
Accurate FEP requires the MTP to reproduce the ab initio phase-space distribution.
Solid TaVCrW has local chemical SRO stabilized at approximately 800 K.
SRO stabilizes TaVCrW by approximately 2-3 meV/atom relative to a random solid solution.
The MTP will be trained on DFT data covering Ta, V, Cr, and W systems.
The relevant validation temperature range is 2000-2400 K.
A supercell containing at least 500 atoms is required to capture SRO correlations.
The calculations will use GGA-PBE with explicit treatment of electronic excitations near the Fermi level.
The MTP can reproduce SRO-dependent local configurations with near-DFT accuracy.
The MTP can reproduce electronic density-of-states features relevant to melting.
Reproducing the ab initio phase-space distribution enables accurate FEP free-energy differences without TI sampling.
MTPs provide near-DFT accuracy with a favorable balance between accuracy and computational cost.
The reduced cost of MTP evaluation permits extensive sampling of solid and liquid coexistence.
FEP computes free-energy differences directly from phase-space overlap and bypasses the slow convergence of TI.
Training on diverse configurations allows the MTP to capture the 2-3 meV/atom SRO stabilization and electronic-excitation-induced melting shifts of tens of kelvin.
The MTP training set must include V and Cr configurations at 0 K to avoid errors associated with underbinding or overbinding.
High-temperature magnetic fluctuations and electronic excitations may cause melting-point shifts not fully captured by the MTP.
GGA-PBE errors for V and Cr at 0 K may propagate into the melting calculation.
The hypothesis is falsified if the MTP+FEP and TOR-TILD solid-liquid free-energy differences on MoNbTaW differ by more than 5 meV/atom.

contradictions.description: The mechanism states that electronic-excitation shifts are captured through MTP training, while the uncertainty field states that electronic excitations may produce shifts not fully captured by the MTP.

The stated objective calls for sub-meV or 0.5 meV/atom agreement, but the proposed falsification criterion permits errors up to 5 meV/atom; this is also looser than the hypothesis's claimed few-meV accuracy.
